manifest.name: dsh-redo
manifest.description: Rewrite the last turn of a DSH session in place: edit a cancelled or failed prompt and resend it, keeping the files it already wrote.
manifest.author: Algorandius

scripts.test: node test/reload.cjs && node test/host.cjs && node test/render.cjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-redo bundle layer.
#
# One row: the Host half owns the fork/inspect/redo operations the Chat row
# calls. No `config` block — the feature has no tunable worth a patch edit.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-redo
      name: 'dsh-redo'

readme.text:
[中文](README.zh.md) | English

Rewrite the last turn of a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) session in place.

Send a prompt, watch it go the wrong way, press stop. This plugin adds a row to that turn so you can edit the prompt and send it again — without starting a new conversation, and without losing the files the first attempt already wrote.

- **Edit & resend** — opens an editor pre-filled with the interrupted prompt, attachments included. The edited prompt replaces the old one in the same conversation.
- **Previous** — a read-only record of the attempt that was replaced: its prompt, why it stopped, and which files it touched.

There is no second session and nothing is added to the sidebar. The arrow is not a navigator: opening the old branch for a glance would litter the sidebar with conversations, so the record is shown inline instead.

1. **The old turn is cancelled.** The same path the stop button uses (`sessionController.cancel`). Without it a still-running turn keeps thinking and writing while the edited prompt is already in flight. It is a no-op on an idle agent, so it runs unconditionally.
2. **The replaced range is shadowed on the model-visible surface.** A `user/message` with `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }` covers the old prompt through the last node that turn produced — the same mechanism compaction uses. The model stops seeing that attempt and stops paying tokens for it. It is appended *before* the new prompt, so the new turn's own prompt stays its prompt.
3. **The replaced rows are hidden in the transcript.** Matched by `data-chat-turn` inside the current session's conversation element, so no other conversation is affected.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Does it still cost context? | No. It is shadowed out of the model-visible surface. |
| Is it deleted? | No. The log is append-only and Harness has no physical delete. |
| Where is it? | Still in `$DSH_HOME/sessions/.../session.v*.jsonl.zstd`, just no longer projected into model messages. |
| Why not delete it for real? | Fork, replay, export and audit all read that log. Compaction shadows ranges for the same reason. |
| Are my files affected? | No. Only what the model sees changes; the workspace is never touched. |
The panel states which case applies to each replacement, so you can tell a real context drop from a failed one.

The repository is installable as a DSH bundle:

```sh
dsh plugin add <this repository>
```

Requires a Harness build that exposes `sessionController.cancel`, `sessionController.prompt` and `session.append`.

| Situation | Row shows |
| --- | --- |
| Stopped by you (`aborted`) | Edit & resend |
| Failed (`error`) | Edit & resend |
| Process interrupted (`interrupted`) | Edit & resend |
| Output limit (`max-tokens`) | Edit & resend |
| Still running | Edit & resend — it stops the turn first |
| Completed normally | Nothing |
| Not the last turn | Nothing |

Only the last turn can be rewritten. An earlier one would have to discard everything after it, which this plugin never does silently.

- `test/host.cjs` — 48 checks. Mounts the Host half in a stub that reproduces Cordis's property trap, then exercises the full redo path against a synthetic session, including the open-turn, failed-prompt and concurrent-redo paths.
- `test/reload.cjs` — 9 checks. Replays the log through the real `adoptSessionEvent` and `foldSurface`, which is where a malformed stored message takes the whole session down. Skips itself when `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` is not installed.
- `test/render.cjs` — 52 checks. Renders the row through a minimal React runtime: conditional states, the editor, drag and drop, context hiding, contrast.
- `test/e2e.cjs` — scans the local session store and reports which turns the plugin would treat as redoable.
- `test/changes.cjs` — checks the changed-file extraction against a real log.
`test/e2e.cjs` and `test/changes.cjs` read `$DSH_HOME/sessions` and skip when it is absent.

**Do not read services as properties.** Cordis installs a trap on the context proxy: reading any property not declared in `inject` throws `cannot get property "X" without inject`, and because it is a getter, `?.` does not guard it. A stray `ctx.sessions` propagates to the chat row, so the error appears under every turn in every conversation. Use `ctx.get('name')`, which returns `undefined` instead.
**Cancel before resending.** Sending a new prompt without stopping the old turn leaves both running; that was a real bug here.

**An appended `user/message` needs an `id`.** The stored log is validated when it is *loaded*, not when an event is appended. One message without an identity makes the whole Session unopenable (`session event at seq N lacks an identified message`), and nothing looks wrong at the time. The shadow message gets one from `randomUUID()`, and `shadowProblem()` re-checks that rule together with the replacement-range rules before anything is written; when it fails the turn is simply left in context.
